newsitem.title: USA: Danaher begins hostile tender for Exide.
newsitem.headline: Danaher begins hostile tender for Exide.

text.p: Danaher Corp., spurned in an attempt at a friendly takeover of Exide Electronics Group Inc., on Wednesday began a hostile tender offer for the maker of power supply systems and management software.
Danaher began its $20-per-share tender offer for Exide after its friendly overtures, including one for $22 a share, were rejected by Exide's board.
The $20-a-share bid would total about $202 million for all of Exide's 10.1 million outstanding shares. However, the company also has about $220 million in outstanding debt.
Exide's stock shot up $7.875 to $20.75 in late trading on the Nasdaq market while Danaher was unchanged at $49.81 on the New York Stock Exchange.
In announcing the tender offer, Washington-based Danaher said it was disappointed that Exide refused to consider its friendly offer, which was made June 11.

"While we continue to strongly prefer a negotiated transaction, in light of the responses from your board of directors, we feel compelled to pursue this matter more expeditiously," Danaher said in a letter to Exide that it made public in announcing the tender offer.
The offensive also includes calling an Exide shareholder meeting and filing a lawsuit to force a transaction.
Danaher, which makes tools, environmental controls and transportation products, said it already owns about 397,000 of Exide's 10.1 million shares.
Duquense Enterprises, the strategic investment unit of the Pittsburg-based utility DQE Inc., owns 1.1 million Exide shares, or about 10.9 percent.
